boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named University of Denver destinations for studying, meeting, services, recreation, and performances.

cards.title: Set up a group-study session at Anderson Academic Commons
cards.subtitle: Main library · 2150 E. Evans Ave.
cards.notes: Use the group study rooms or computers between classes, then consult the library’s floor map when you need a specific room or service.
cards.short_summary: DU’s main library combines collections, computers, academic support, and group-study space.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Denver identifies Anderson Academic Commons as its main library and says it provides group study rooms and computers.
cards.source_title: Living at DU | University of Denver
cards.access_notes: Library floor maps and room information are available through University Libraries.

cards.title: Meet up in the Community Commons
cards.subtitle: 2055 E. Evans Ave. · student activity hub
cards.notes: Use the communal spaces or reservable rooms for a planned meetup, and check the building page before relying on seasonal hours.
cards.short_summary: A four-floor campus hub with dining, gathering areas, student services, and event spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Affairs describes Community Commons as a central hub of student activity with dining, social spaces, reservable meeting rooms, and services.
cards.access_notes: Student Affairs posts building hours that vary by academic period and break.

cards.title: Use Driscoll Commons as a service stop
cards.subtitle: 2050 E. Evans Ave. · connected to Community Commons
cards.notes: Plan one practical errand here, such as an ID question, accessibility support, bookstore visit, or Food Pantry stop; confirm office availability first.
cards.short_summary: The connected commons building concentrates several student-facing services.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Affairs lists the DU Food Pantry, Pioneer ID Card Office, Student Disability Services, bookstore, and bank among Driscoll Commons services.
cards.access_notes: Individual offices and the bookstore maintain their own availability; consult the department listing before visiting.

cards.title: Take a breather in the Undergraduate Lounge
cards.subtitle: Community Commons 3600 · third floor
cards.notes: Bring a friend for a low-key pause between commitments, and treat the lounge as a shared student space rather than a reservable meeting room.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated third-floor respite and social space for undergraduate students.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Affairs says the Undergraduate Lounge in Community Commons 3600 is for undergraduates to mingle, socialize, and connect.
cards.access_notes: Located on the third floor of Community Commons; intended for undergraduate students.

cards.title: Connect with peers in the Graduate Lounge
cards.subtitle: Community Commons 3800 · third floor
cards.notes: Use this graduate-focused lounge for a short reset or conversation with peers, keeping the space available for the wider graduate community.
cards.short_summary: A designated Community Commons space for graduate-student respite and connection.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Affairs identifies the Graduate Lounge in Community Commons 3800 as a place for graduate students to socialize and connect.
cards.access_notes: Located on the third floor of Community Commons; intended for graduate students.

cards.title: Locate the DU Food Pantry before you need it
cards.subtitle: Driscoll Commons, Garden Level, Suite 6
cards.notes: Save the suite location now, then visit the Food Pantry’s official page for eligibility, appointment, and current access information before going.
cards.short_summary: A named campus pantry located in Driscoll Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Affairs lists the DU Food Pantry on the Garden Level of Driscoll Commons in Suite 6.
cards.access_notes: Check the Food Pantry’s current program information before visiting.

cards.title: Put the Burwell Center on your career-planning route
cards.subtitle: 2190 E. Asbury Ave. · campus career destination
cards.notes: Use the campus-listed location as a waypoint when arranging career support, and confirm the relevant program or appointment details before arrival.
cards.short_summary: A named campus destination for career achievement services.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Denver’s campus map lists the Burwell Center for Career Achievement, and the registrar gives its address as 2190 E. Asbury Ave.
cards.access_notes: Use the Career Achievement office’s current instructions for appointments and service availability.

cards.entity_name: Newman Center for the Performing Arts
cards.title: Check the Newman Center calendar for a performance
cards.subtitle: 2344 E. Iliff Ave. · Lamont School of Music & Theatre
cards.notes: Browse the current Lamont calendar, then review the individual event’s ticketing details before heading to the Newman Center.
cards.short_summary: A campus performance venue that hosts Lamont School of Music & Theatre events.
cards.evidence_claim: DU identifies the Newman Center as the Lamont School of Music & Theatre location and directs visitors to its performance calendar and box office.
cards.source_title: Lamont School of Music & Theatre Events Calendar
cards.access_notes: Some Lamont concerts are free while others are ticketed; verify the specific event before attending.

cards.entity_name: Daniel L. Ritchie Center for Sports and Wellness
cards.title: Make the Ritchie Center part of an active day
cards.subtitle: 2201 E. Asbury Ave. · sports and wellness facility
cards.notes: Use the official campus map to orient yourself, then check the relevant recreation, club-sport, or event information before planning your visit.
cards.short_summary: A named campus facility associated with sports, wellness, club sports, and intramurals.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Denver’s campus resources identify the Ritchie Center in connection with Pioneer Athletics, Coors Fitness Center, club sports, and intramurals.
cards.access_notes: Programs, memberships, and event access may have separate requirements; consult the relevant Ritchie Center program page.

cards.title: Pause at Evans Chapel during a campus walk
cards.subtitle: University of Denver campus · map-listed chapel
cards.notes: Include the chapel as a quiet landmark on a walking route, and check campus event information if you intend to attend a scheduled program.
cards.short_summary: A named chapel and campus landmark on the University of Denver map.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Denver’s official campus map lists Evans Chapel as a campus destination.
cards.access_notes: Access may vary when the chapel is reserved or used for scheduled programs.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission, no-purchase activities on and around the University of Denver campus, with access details for planning a low-key outing.

cards.title: See a rotating visual-art exhibition
cards.subtitle: Shwayder Art Building, 2121 E. Asbury Ave.
cards.notes: Meet at the Shwayder Art Building and browse the current exhibition together; check the gallery page before going because exhibitions and building access can change.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission gallery visit with changing student and professional work.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission is always free at the Vicki Myhren Gallery, which is located in DU's Shwayder Art Building.
cards.access_notes: When exhibitions are up, listed hours are 12–5 p.m. Tuesday–Friday; DU building access may require a University ID or advance coordination for visitors.

cards.title: Visit the student-run Davis Gallery
cards.subtitle: Shwayder Art Building, 2121 E. Asbury Ave.
cards.notes: Pair this with the neighboring Vicki Myhren Gallery, then pause to compare one work each; verify the current exhibition schedule before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A student-run exhibition space sharing the Shwayder Art Building's main floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission is always free at Davis Gallery, located on the main floor of Shwayder Art Building at the University of Denver.
cards.access_notes: When exhibitions are up, listed hours are 12–5 p.m. Tuesday–Friday; DU building access may require a University ID or advance coordination for visitors.

cards.title: Browse the library's public exhibits
cards.subtitle: Anderson Academic Commons, 2150 E. Evans Ave.
cards.notes: Walk the three levels and pick an exhibit to discuss; displays change each quarter, so use the current-exhibits page to choose a timely stop.
cards.short_summary: Library exhibits spanning art, scholarship, and materials from DU collections.
cards.evidence_claim: All University Libraries exhibits are open to the public and are located in public areas on all three levels of Anderson Academic Commons.
cards.access_notes: A valid DU ID is required to enter campus buildings, including the library.

cards.title: Take a self-guided tree walk
cards.subtitle: Meet at the Mary Reed Building information kiosk
cards.notes: Download or pick up the Tree Walk Guide, then wander the gardens at your own pace while keeping to the Arboretum's passive-appreciation rules.
cards.short_summary: A campus arboretum with a free self-guided route through its plant collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The Chester M. Alter Arboretum is free and open to the public 365 days a year, and self-guided tours are available at no charge.
cards.access_notes: Information kiosk: southwest corner of Mary Reed Building, 2199 S. University Blvd. Follow Arboretum rules and do not pick or damage plants.

cards.entity_name: Chester M. Alter Arboretum guided walking tour
cards.title: Book a free guided garden walk
cards.subtitle: Chester M. Alter Arboretum; May–September group tours
cards.notes: Gather a garden club, residence-hall group, or friends and request a guided walk; wear comfortable shoes, sun protection, and bring water for grassy areas.
cards.short_summary: An hour-long guided introduction to DU's gardens, collections, and Arboretum history.
cards.evidence_claim: All guided Chester M. Alter Arboretum tours are free of charge and are offered May through September.
cards.access_notes: Tours meet at the Arboretum information kiosk by Mary Reed Building; reservations and seasonal availability apply.

cards.title: Follow DU's campus art walking tour
cards.subtitle: Outdoor and indoor art installations across campus
cards.notes: Download the tour before setting out, choose a few stops that interest the group, and keep the route flexible around building-access requirements.
cards.short_summary: A self-paced way to locate artworks installed around the University of Denver campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Vicki Myhren Gallery provides a downloadable campus art walking tour for art installations around DU.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor works are the simplest option; some campus buildings require a valid DU ID or advance visitor coordination.

cards.entity_name: Lamont School of Music free recitals
cards.title: Choose a free recital or student show
cards.subtitle: Lamont School of Music and DU recital halls
cards.notes: Check the current arts calendar, invite a friend, and select a recital or small student show marked free; confirm any ticket or reservation detail before leaving.
cards.short_summary: Recurring free performances from DU's campus arts scene.
cards.evidence_claim: DU states that its campus arts scene includes dozens of free recitals and small student shows every month.
cards.access_notes: Individual events may have their own schedules or free-ticket requirements; check the event listing before attending.

cards.title: Cheer at a DU basketball game
cards.subtitle: Student ticket offer; verify the current schedule
cards.notes: Use the student-ticket offer for a basketball game, coordinate seats with friends, and review the athletics schedule and entry instructions before game day.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost student-ticket option for supporting DU basketball.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Denver states that students can take advantage of free student tickets for sports such as basketball.
cards.access_notes: For DU students; ticket availability, schedule, and venue entry procedures should be confirmed with athletics before attending.

cards.title: Go to a DU volleyball match
cards.subtitle: Student ticket offer; verify the current schedule
cards.notes: Plan around the current volleyball schedule and claim the student ticket before the match; meeting up beforehand makes it an easy group outing.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost student-ticket option for watching DU volleyball.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Denver states that students can take advantage of free student tickets for sports such as volleyball.
cards.access_notes: For DU students; ticket availability, schedule, and venue entry procedures should be confirmed with athletics before attending.

cards.title: Join a Mountain Campus program
cards.subtitle: DU's 720-acre mountain campus, about two hours from Denver
cards.notes: Look for a student program that includes Mountain Campus access, then plan the trip with the sponsoring office; follow program guidance for transport, gear, and conditions.
cards.short_summary: A DU mountain-campus setting available to students without an extra access charge.
cards.evidence_claim: DU describes its 720-acre James C. Kennedy Mountain Campus as accessible to all students at no extra cost.
cards.access_notes: Access is through DU student opportunities; confirm the sponsoring program's transportation, timing, and any required equipment before participating.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented University of Denver traditions, from historic campus rituals to recurring student-led celebrations.

cards.title: See the DU Rose
cards.subtitle: University of Denver campus tradition
cards.notes: Look for Rosa Denvera at university functions and use the official history to connect the flower to DU’s 1912 campus story.
cards.short_summary: A distinct rose variety developed from a bush gifted to the University in 1912.
cards.evidence_claim: DU identifies the DU Rose as Rosa Denvera, developed after botanist Ira Cutler found the 1912 gift’s blossoms unlike any others; it is still used for campus functions.
cards.access_notes: Look for the rose at scheduled university functions; availability varies by event.

cards.title: Join the Founders Celebration
cards.subtitle: University of Denver community tradition
cards.notes: Check the university’s announcements for Founders Celebration lectures, forums, and gatherings that honor people who shaped DU.
cards.short_summary: A recurring commemoration of the people and vision that have influenced the University.
cards.evidence_claim: DU describes Founders Celebration as a treasured tradition dating to its earliest days, with lectures, forums, and gatherings honoring contributors to the University.
cards.access_notes: Programming and participation details vary by year; consult current university announcements.

cards.title: Watch for First Snow
cards.subtitle: University of Denver campus tradition
cards.notes: When Denver’s first snowfall arrives, check Student Affairs and CrimsonConnect for the current campus celebration details.
cards.short_summary: A DU-specific seasonal celebration tied to the first snow of the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Denver Student Affairs names First Snow among the institution’s unique campus traditions.
cards.access_notes: Occurs only when seasonal conditions and organizers support a current event; check official listings.

cards.title: Take Part in DU Homecoming
cards.subtitle: University of Denver alumni and student tradition
cards.notes: Use the official Homecoming schedule to choose a public activity, such as the Crimson Classic or an alumni-community gathering.
cards.short_summary: A DU reunion tradition that links current students, alumni, families, and the hockey program.
cards.evidence_claim: DU documents Homecoming as a tradition more than 100 years old; after football ended in 1960, Homecoming support centered on hockey and the Colorado College rivalry.
cards.access_notes: Held on scheduled Homecoming dates; event access and registration requirements vary.

cards.title: Follow Winter Carnival
cards.subtitle: DU Programming Board winter tradition
cards.notes: Review DUPB’s current Winter Carnival listing for on-campus events, then decide separately whether any mountain-weekend options fit your plans.
cards.short_summary: A week-long DU winter tradition begun in 1961, with campus programming and mountain activities.
cards.evidence_claim: DU Programming Board says Winter Carnival began in 1961 and is a week-long DU tradition, with on-campus events followed by a mountain weekend.
cards.access_notes: On-campus and mountain portions have separate current details; some mountain activities may require registration or payment.

cards.title: Plan Around May Days
cards.subtitle: DU Programming Board spring tradition
cards.notes: Check DUPB’s schedule near spring finals for the week’s campus activities and any MusicFest details before heading out.
cards.short_summary: DU’s longest-running tradition is a spring week of outdoor events and entertainment.
cards.evidence_claim: DU states that May Days dates to 1913 and is its longest-running tradition; it takes place at the end of spring quarter before finals.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled at the end of spring quarter; individual activities and access requirements vary.

cards.title: Follow Hockey Night Lights
cards.subtitle: Formerly Hockey Campout at DU
cards.notes: Watch DUPB and Athletics announcements for the current Hockey Night Lights format and ticket information before making plans.
cards.short_summary: A DU hockey-season tradition founded in 2001 and formerly called Hockey Campout.
cards.evidence_claim: DU Programming Board records that Hockey Night Lights, formerly Hockey Campout, was founded in 2001.
cards.access_notes: Format, date, and ticket eligibility are announced for each season; verify current DUPB and Athletics information.

cards.title: Track Munch Week
cards.subtitle: DU Programming Board food tradition
cards.notes: Check CrimsonConnect for the day’s Munch Week location and timing, then stop by for the listed snack distribution.
cards.short_summary: A recurring campus food week that places free snacks around DU during the academic term.
cards.evidence_claim: DU describes Munch Week as a week-long celebration with free snacks across campus; another DU guide says it occurs each quarter and is supported by local businesses.
cards.access_notes: Locations, quantities, and timing vary by current event listing; availability can be limited.

cards.title: Catch Battle of the Bands
cards.subtitle: DU Programming Board student-music tradition
cards.notes: Follow DUPB’s event listing for performers and venue, then see which student acts compete for the MusicFest opening slot.
cards.short_summary: An annual student performance competition whose winner earns a MusicFest opening opportunity.
cards.evidence_claim: DU identifies Battle of the Bands as an annual student-talent showcase; its winner earns the opportunity to open at MusicFest.
cards.access_notes: Venue, performers, and attendance details are set for each annual event; consult DUPB’s current listing.

cards.title: Recognize Profiles of Excellence
cards.subtitle: University of Denver student-to-alum tradition
cards.notes: Look for the current Profiles of Excellence program and attend or support the ceremony recognizing graduating students of color.
cards.short_summary: A long-running DU ceremony marking the transition of students of color from student to alum.
cards.evidence_claim: DU Student Affairs says Profiles of Excellence has been a campus tradition for more than 20 years and commemorates the journey of students of color from student to alum.
cards.access_notes: Ceremony timing and participation information vary annually; check Student Affairs for current details.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Denver, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure, under-21-safe sequence of campus landmarks, student resources, and recurring cultural options for getting oriented.

cards.title: Start at the Community Commons
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · campus orientation stop
cards.notes: Meet your group in the central student hub, then use its dining, gathering, and student-service spaces to decide the rest of the weekend.
cards.short_summary: A practical first meeting point with food, lounges, and student services in one building.
cards.evidence_claim: DU describes Community Commons as a central hub for student activity with dining, social spaces, meeting rooms, and student services.
cards.access_notes: Campus destination; check building access and individual venue availability before visiting.

cards.title: Have a first campus meal together
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Community Commons
cards.notes: Use the central dining hall as an easy regrouping stop; check the current menu and service status before choosing a meal.
cards.short_summary: DU’s central campus dining hall is built into Community Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: DU identifies the Rebecca Chopp Grand Central Market as the central campus dining hall in Community Commons.
cards.access_notes: Food is purchased or covered through an applicable meal plan; verify current dining service before going.

cards.title: Cross the Evans Pedestrian Bridge
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · between Community Commons and Driscoll Commons
cards.notes: Walk the named bridge between the two commons buildings and use the crossing to orient yourself to Evans Avenue and campus services.
cards.short_summary: A named pedestrian connection linking DU’s two commons buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: DU states that the Evans Pedestrian Bridge connects Driscoll Commons and Community Commons.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor pedestrian route; use normal campus pedestrian safety practices.

cards.title: Find the main library before classes begin
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · campus study stop
cards.notes: Locate the main library, identify an entrance and a study floor, and save it as a dependable place for your first academic week.
cards.short_summary: The map-listed main library gives a new student a useful academic anchor.
cards.evidence_claim: DU’s campus map lists Anderson Academic Commons as the Main Library.
cards.access_notes: Confirm library access and service hours on the University Libraries website before planning a long study session.

cards.title: Add Buchtel Memorial Tower to your walk
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · campus landmark stop
cards.notes: Use the tower as a recognizable waypoint while walking the academic core, then continue toward nearby library and classroom buildings.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed campus landmark that helps make the central walk legible.
cards.evidence_claim: DU’s campus map lists Buchtel Memorial Tower among campus buildings and greens.
cards.access_notes: View from public outdoor areas; do not assume interior access.

cards.title: Pause at Evans Chapel
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · campus landmark stop
cards.notes: Include the chapel on a daylight campus loop and note its location for future ceremonies, quiet reflection, or a photo with friends.
cards.short_summary: A named campus chapel on DU’s official map.
cards.evidence_claim: DU’s campus map lists Evans Chapel as a campus destination.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is the reliable plan; confirm whether the chapel is open before seeking indoor access.

cards.title: Try a recreation session at Coors
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Daniel L. Ritchie Center
cards.notes: Bring your Pioneer ID, ask the front desk about student entry, and choose a simple activity such as open recreation or lap swimming.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation facility offering fitness, open basketball, lap swimming, and other activities.
cards.evidence_claim: DU says actively enrolled students may use Coors Fitness Center and lists group fitness, open recreation basketball, and open lap swimming.
cards.access_notes: Full-time students in the current term are eligible for free access and must use a DU ID to sign in; confirm activity schedules first.

cards.entity_name: Robert and Judi Newman Center for the Performing Arts
cards.title: Check the Newman Center calendar
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · performance option
cards.notes: Look for a performance that fits your weekend and reserve only if the listed program, ticket availability, and timing work for your group.
cards.short_summary: A campus performing-arts venue with a published presenting-season lineup.
cards.evidence_claim: DU publishes a Newman Center Presents season and directs visitors to purchase tickets and season passes for listed performances.
cards.source_title: Newman Center Unveils Lineup for 2026–27 Season | University of Denver
cards.access_notes: Admission, age guidance, and performance times vary by event; use the current event listing before making plans.

cards.title: Plan a Chamberlin Observatory open house
cards.subtitle: Saturday night · Observatory Park
cards.notes: Check the Denver Astronomical Society schedule, then attend a monthly lawn open house when it aligns with your weekend instead of arriving unannounced.
cards.short_summary: A DU-operated observatory near campus with recurring public astronomy outreach.
cards.evidence_claim: DU says Chamberlin Observatory’s monthly open houses include free lawn telescopes and require no registration.
cards.access_notes: Monthly open houses are free and need no registration; public nights have limited seats and require advance registration, with pricing set by the host.

cards.title: Finish by locating Driscoll Commons services
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · practical campus reset
cards.notes: Walk through Driscoll Commons and note the Food Pantry, Pioneer ID Card Office, disability services, and bookstore for future reference.
cards.short_summary: A service-focused commons building connected to Community Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: DU lists the Food Pantry, Pioneer ID Card Office, Student Disability Services, bookstore, and bank among Driscoll Commons services.
cards.access_notes: Service availability varies by office; verify individual office hours before making a special trip.
